name: Container home community
summary: Homes built from converted shipping containers (typically 1-2 forty-foot high-cube boxes, 320-640 SF) set on piers or slabs with individual utility hookups, plus shared roads, parking and landscaping. The container shell is cheap but conversion (cutting, reinforcement, spray-foam insulation, windows, MEP) and code compliance bring $/SF close to small conventional homes. Only consumer cost-guide data was retrieved in this session; the community default is derived. Confidence low.

typicalSize.method: Judgment: container housing communities and supportive projects typically 10-40 homes.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Bob Vila size table: 320 SF = 1 or 2 containers (1 bed, 1 bath); 1,280 SF = 4 containers (x1). Mid 640 SF = two 40-ft containers; high three.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Detached small homes on a shared site behave like cottage courts (gross 10-31 du/acre, cottage-court k1); container homes are smaller, mid 14.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Judgment; supportive projects lower, market-rate ~1 per home.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Home + site build-up. Home: Bob Vila prefab container homes $150-$300/SF, custom $250-$400/SF; 320 SF (1-2 containers) $25k-$82k; 1,280 SF (4 containers) $150k-$220k (x1, x2). Mid home = 640 SF x ~$225/SF (midpoint of prefab range; site-installed, code-compliant) = ~$144k. Site per home ~$40k: foundation $3,000-$19,350 (x3), utility connections, shared roads/parking, landscaping, crane set - benchmarked to the tiny-home pad infrastructure (~$45k mid, tiny-home-community). Mid = ~$185k. Low = 320 SF single container at ~$200/SF ($64k) + $30k site; high = 960 SF custom at ~$300/SF (~$290k) + $40k site. Consumer-guide data only; verify with modular/container builder bids.

perSF.method: perPrimaryUnit / sfPerPrimaryUnit (95k/320 ~ $297 is skewed by fixed site cost; 185k/640 = $289; 330k/960 = $344); low set at $230 to reflect larger economy units. Includes site work.

scope.notes: Contractor/manufacturer price incl. container conversion, delivery and crane set, foundation, finishes, MEP, and on-site work (grading, roads, parking, utilities, landscaping), incl. general conditions and OH&P. Excludes land, soft costs, FF&E, off-site utilities, tap/impact fees.

systemSplit.method: Started from the cottage-court split (NAHB stage shares, cottage-court k3) and moved framing to Div 05 (container shell, cutting, steel reinforcement, lintels ~12%) with a smaller 06 for interior framing; foundations reduced (piers); spray-foam/roofing 07; site/utility share ~23% (31+32+33) because units are small.

lineItems.name: 40-ft high-cube container shell, cutouts and steel reinforcement

cost.method: Judgment: used/one-trip high-cube container ($3k-$7k) plus cutting, framing of openings and reinforcement. No source retrieved; verify with suppliers.
Bob Vila: container home foundation $3,000-$19,350 on average (x3).
Judgment: trucking plus crane day rate shared across containers set per day.

lineItems.name: Per-home utility connections (electric, water line, sewer)

cost.method: Bob Vila: electrical grid connection $250-$1,500, water line $32-$53/LF (x4); community-scale laterals per RV/tiny-home pad (~$9k, rv e8).
Bob Vila single-home septic $3,300-$5,000 (x4) is a floor; community system scaled from RV park evidence (~$100k small park, rv e14). Judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Unfurnished for sale/long-term rent; high if furnished (STR or supportive housing).

pctOfHard.method: Judgment: structural engineering of modified containers, code approval (often alternative-materials review or state modular approval), site civil, permits. Higher than conventional because approvals are less routine.

softCosts.notes: Third-party inspection for factory-built modules may apply.

design.method: Judgment; code-approval risk for non-standard construction.

hard.method: Judgment; container condition and rust/remediation risk.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Min = single-container home + basic site + low soft; max = 3-container custom home ($400/SF, x2) + site + soft.
